questions.text: What is the course code for IT Project Management, per the course presentation?
questions.explanation: The course plan lists the code as FELEC P, worth 3.0 Academic Units.

questions.text: How many academic units is the IT Project Management course worth?
questions.explanation: The course is listed as 3.0 Academic Units.

questions.text: What is the prerequisite for taking this course?
questions.explanation: The listed prerequisite is 3rd Year Standing.

questions.text: Match each Course Intended Learning Outcome (CILO) to what it focuses on.
questions.explanation: CILO 1 covers success/failure factors, CILO 2 covers best practices, CILO 3 covers the 10 PMBOK Knowledge Areas, and CILO 4 covers deliverable analysis.

questions.text: CILO 3 requires students to demonstrate mastery of PMBOK's ___ Knowledge Areas across all 5 project process stages.
questions.explanation: CILO 3 states: "Demonstrate mastery of PMBOK's 10 Knowledge Areas across all 5 project process stages."

questions.text: Which CILO is mapped to Program Outcomes IT05 and IT09?
questions.explanation: CILO 1 (Success & Failure Factors) is mapped to IT05, IT09.

questions.text: Under "The Role of the IT Project Manager," which responsibility covers ensuring project artifacts align with system design requirements without scope creep?
questions.explanation: Scope & Integration Control ensures project artifacts align with system design requirements without scope creep.

questions.text: Which PMBOK process group, per the semester roadmap, covers defining project scope, selecting projects via financial criteria, and establishing the Project Charter?
questions.explanation: Initiating covers defining scope, project selection, and the Project Charter.

questions.text: Which process group covers developing the WBS, RTM, schedule baseline, cost estimates, and comprehensive risk management plans?
questions.explanation: Planning covers the WBS, RTM, schedule baseline, cost estimates, and risk management plans.

questions.text: Which process group covers coordinating software engineering teams, managing stakeholders, and implementing quality control?
questions.explanation: Executing covers coordinating teams, managing stakeholders, and quality control.

questions.text: Which process group covers tracking schedule performance, processing change requests, and applying Quality Control tools?
questions.explanation: Monitoring covers tracking schedule performance, change requests, and QC tools.

questions.text: In the Prelim Grade formula, what weight is given to the Prelim Exam?
questions.explanation: Prelim Grade = (Long Test 1 & 2 - 25%) + (Prelim Exam - 40%) + (Deliverables - 25%) + (Attendance - 10%).

questions.text: The Final Grade is calculated as 50% Prelim Grade + 50% Tentative Final Grade.
questions.explanation: The course plan states: Final Grade = 50% Prelim Grade + 50% Tentative Final Grade.

questions.text: Per the UST Transmutation Table, what percentage range corresponds to a grade of 1.00?
questions.explanation: A grade of 1.00 (Excellent) corresponds to 96% - 100%.

questions.text: What is the minimum passing percentage under the UST transmutation system?
questions.explanation: A grade of 3.00 (Passed, Minimum Passing) corresponds to 75% - 78%.

questions.text: According to the 18-week semester roadmap, which weeks cover Integration, Stakeholders, WBS, RTM, and Prelim Examinations?
questions.explanation: Weeks 4-8 cover Integration, Stakeholders, WBS, RTM & Prelim Examinations.

questions.text: Which weeks cover Quality Management, the 7 QC Tools, and Risk Identification & Matrix?
questions.explanation: Weeks 10-14 cover Quality Management, 7 QC Tools, Risk Identification & Matrix.

questions.text: Which of the following are explicitly listed among the course's Quality Control techniques?
questions.explanation: The listed QC techniques are Fishbone Diagrams, Pareto Analysis & Histograms, Scatter Diagrams & Flowcharts, and the Seven Run Rule & Six Sigma Principles. SWOT Analysis is not mentioned.

questions.text: Which core project deliverable includes formal initiation authorization, scope statements, and the WBS dictionary?
questions.explanation: The Project Charter & WBS deliverable includes formal initiation authorization, scope statements, and the WBS dictionary.

questions.text: The CICS Good Grooming Policy, requiring compliance with dress code and uniform guidelines, is part of the course's class policies.
questions.explanation: The class policies list "CICS Good Grooming Policy: Strict compliance with the College of Information and Computing Sciences dress code and uniform guidelines."
